newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Delayed supplies for Mir station launched - Interfax.
newsitem.headline: Delayed supplies for Mir station launched - Interfax.

text.p: Russia launched a freight satellite early on Wednesday to deliver supplies to the three crew of its orbitting Mir space station, Interfax news agency reported.

The mission was delayed for more than a month, mainly due to financial problems holding up production of the Soyuz-U booster rocket and Russia is still smarting from the embarrassing loss of its Mars-96 mission at the weekend..
The Progress M-33 freight satellite was sent aloft aboard a Soyuz-U rocket at 2:20 a.m. (2320 GMT on Tuesday) from Baykonur cosmodrome in Kazakhstan.
It was carrying scientific equipment, fuel, oxygen, water, food, instruments and parcels for the Mir crew and it was expected to dock 48 hours after being launched.

The Mir crew -- cosmonauts Valery Korzun and Alexander Koleri and U.S. astronaut John Blaha -- had been due to be relieved in mid-December. But cash problems has forced the postponement of the launch of the next crew, including a German, until February.
Blaha and his two Russian colleagues have been aboard Mir station since September 19. Four Mir launches have been held up this year because of money troubles in the Russian space industry.
The unmanned Mars-96 probe, which crashed into the sea off Chile on Monday just over a day after lift-off, was launched two years late due to a lack of state funds.
Around $300 million worth of work and equipment was lost when the stricken craft failed to break out of Earth's orbit.
A faulty Proton booster is thought to have caused the crash.
But some officials have said shortage of cash for Russia's prestigious space programme was at the root of the calamity.
